Tweaks.WeaponPosePerJob.Title: Weapon Poses
Tweaks.WeaponPosePerJob.Help.Title: Help
Tweaks.WeaponPosePerJob.Help.Text:
The game keeps a single weapon-drawn pose for all jobs. This tweak remembers one for each job.

To save a pose: draw your weapon and use /cpose until you like it. It is saved for your current job automatically.

When you switch to a job with a saved pose, it is put back as soon as you draw your weapon outside of combat.

"Default" means no pose has been saved for that job yet.
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Name: GoblinSniper
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Description: Watches the market board for listings priced far below what the item normally sells for (like a mount posted at 100,000 gil instead of 1,000,000) and lists them. The number of deals found is shown in the Server Info Bar.
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Language.Help: Language of the item names in the window and in the search below. Independent of the GoblinTweaks language; defaults to it.
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Notify: Show in the Server Info Bar
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Notify.Help: Adds an entry with the number of deals found. Click it to open the window.
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.WholeDataCenter.Help: Looks at every world of your data center, not only your home world. You have to visit the world to buy.
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Discount.Help: The listing has to be at least this much below the normal price, and below the next seller.
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.MinPrice.Help: Items that normally sell for less than this are ignored.
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.MaxAge.Help: Ignores listings whose price was uploaded longer ago than this. Lower means fewer but more reliable deals.
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.MaxDays.Help: Ignores items that nobody bought for more than this many days: they would just sit on the market.
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Types.Help: Every marketable item of the selected types is watched. The number is how many items each type adds; the big ones (weapons, armor, furnishings) make every scan take a few minutes.
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Items.Help: Watch individual items of any type. Search by name and click a result to add it.
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Sort.Name: Name

Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Help.Title: Help
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Help.About.Title: What it does
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Help.About.Text:
GoblinSniper looks for listings priced far below what the item normally sells for. Most of the time the seller made a typo: a mount posted at 100,000 gil instead of 1,000,000.

A listing counts as a deal only if all of this is true:

- It is below the average price by at least the discount you chose.
- It is also that far below the next seller. If everyone lists low, the price simply dropped.
- The item normally sells for more than your minimum price.
- The data is not older than your maximum data age.
- Someone bought the item recently (60 days by default).

With a low discount (30%) you will mostly see price differences between worlds. Raise it to keep only the real mistakes.
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Help.Columns.Title: Columns
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Help.Columns.Text:
Item: icon, name and type. Hover a row to see the game tooltip. Click a row to copy the item name, then paste it in the search of a market board.

iLvl: the item level.

Avg. price: the average sale price of the last days in the area being scanned. If the item sells rarely, the price of its last sale is used.

Listed price: the cheapest listing right now, in green. Below it, "Next" is the cheapest listing of a different seller.

Discount: how far the listed price is below the average price.

World: where the listing is. To buy it you have to travel to that world.

Updated: how long ago that price was uploaded.
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Help.Resale.Title: Resale chance
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Help.Resale.Text:
The Resale column estimates how likely it is that you can sell the item again on your home world within 7 days.

It comes from "sales per day", the figure Universalis calculates from the sales of the last days, shown under the percentage. With 0.1 sales per day (one every 10 days) the chance is about 50%; with 0.5 per day it is about 97%.

Green is 75% or more, yellow is 40% or more, red is less.

If your world has no recent sales, an even share of the sales of the whole data center is used instead.

It is an estimate: it assumes you list at a price people pay, and it does not know how many other sellers you compete with.

Items that nobody bought for too long are left out of the list: 60 days by default, see "Maximum days without a sale" in the settings. Universalis does not say how long a listing has been up, so this is judged by the last sale of the item.
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Help.Sorting.Title: Sorting and filters
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Help.Sorting.Text:
"Sort by" only changes the order of the list: biggest discount (in %), biggest saving (in gil), lowest price, highest avg. price, item level, name, item type, world, or most recently updated.

The two lists next to it are filters, and they do hide rows:

- World: only the deals of one world. It lists the worlds that have a deal right now.
- Data age: only the deals whose price was uploaded less than 1, 3, 6 or 12 hours ago.

The search box filters by item name or world name.

The small X next to the search box empties it. The round arrow next to the filters sets them back to all worlds and any data age.
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Help.Data.Title: Prices and data age
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Help.Data.Text:
The game cannot be asked for the market board of another world, so prices come from Universalis, a public site that players feed when they open an item on a market board.

That is why data has an age. "Updated: 15h" means nobody has looked at that item on that world for 15 hours, and the listing may already be sold.

The plugin cannot make data newer. You can: travel to that world and open the item on the market board, and it is uploaded right away.

Popular items are refreshed all the time; rare ones can go many hours without an update.

To see only recent data, lower "Maximum data age" in the settings. You will get fewer deals, but more reliable ones.
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Help.Scanning.Title: Scans and alerts
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Help.Scanning.Text:
A scan runs a moment after you log in, every few minutes (see the settings), when you change a setting and when you press the scan button (the arrows, top right). The gear next to it opens the settings.

Deals appear as they are found, without waiting for the scan to end. A deal of the previous scan stays listed until its item is checked again.

The scan button locks until the scan ends, so it cannot be started twice. The bottom bar shows the progress.

The number in the Server Info Bar is how many deals are on the list right now. Click it to open this window; hover it to see the best ones.

If the bottom bar says Universalis is overloaded or did not answer, nothing is wrong on your side. What was found is kept and the scan is retried in a couple of minutes.
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Help.Items.Title: Which items are watched
Tweaks.GoblinSniper.Help.Items.Text:
Only what you choose in the settings is scanned, not the whole game. "Items watched" in the bottom bar is that total.

Item types: mounts, minions, orchestrion rolls, Triple Triad cards, bardings, fashion accessories, hairstyles and emotes, dyes, materia, workshop parts, other collectibles, weapons, armor and furnishings. Each one shows how many items it adds.

Weapons, armor and furnishings have thousands of items, so a scan with them takes a few minutes.

Specific items: search any item by name in the settings and click it to watch it, whatever its type.

Only items that can be sold on the market board are included. The language of the item names is chosen in the settings.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Name: Goblin Battle Text
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Description: Scrolls the damage and healing you deal and receive around the center of the screen, where your character stands, instead of over whoever was hit, and announces buffs, debuffs and cooldowns under it. Every event, area, color and the order of each message is configurable. Type /gbt in chat to open its settings.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Open.Help: Opens the Goblin Battle Text settings window. Sample text scrolls while it is open.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Title: Goblin Battle Text
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Help.Positionals:
Actions that hit harder from the rear or the flank of their target (Gekko, Kasha, Gibbet, Gallows, Fang and Claw...) say whether you hit them from there. Which actions have a positional, and which side, is read from the game's own description of each action: there is no list to keep up to date.

The game does not say whether you hit it. Each hit comes with the share of its potency that is a bonus (combo plus positional), and two things are checked:
- The bonus: the potencies in the description of the action, at your level (synced or not), tell what it should be when the positional is hit and when it is missed.
- Where you stood: the rear is the quarter of the circle behind the enemy, 45° to each side of its back; the flanks are the two quarters at its sides.

The verdict:
- No bonus at all: missed.
- An action with no combo (Gibbet, Trick Attack...): any bonus is the positional, so hit.
- The bonus of a hit: hit.
- The bonus of a miss, or one that was not expected (an effect is raising the potency): where you stood decides.

True North, enemies with no sides and effects that remove them count as hit, as in the game. An action that does no damage says nothing.

Events tab: turn it on or off, choose its area, or show it in the damage message. Highlights tab: its look.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Help.OverTime.Te:
Ticks of damage over time (DoT) and healing over time (HoT) come from the game with no action: one number per target every 3 seconds.

Name and icon: those of the effect that ticks, like 132 Higanbana or +78 Regen. With several effects, all are named. Effects on the ground, like Doton, are named too. When none is found, the tick says (DoT) or (HoT).

Whose it is:
- When the game says who gave it (healing over time, effects on the ground), that is used: you only see yours and those of your pet, and the number is exact.
- When it does not (most damage over time), the game sends one sum of everyone's on that enemy. If none of it is yours, the tick is not shown. If only yours is there, the number is exact. If others have theirs too, your share is an estimate, one part per effect, with ~ before it: ~178 Higanbana.

Where it shows:
- Healing over time on you is healing received, whoever gave it.
- On anyone else, your pet included, it is healing given, and shows only when you or your pet gave it.
- Damage over time on you is damage taken.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Help.Rules.Title: What counts as yours
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Help.Rules.Text:
Debuffs on enemies: only the ones you put. + name when it starts and - name when yours is gone from the enemy; the same debuff from someone of your job is told apart. Nothing is said when the enemy dies.

Pets: with Include my pet and chocobo (General tab), what your chocobo or pet deals, heals and puts on others counts as yours, also when it heals itself.

Counterattacks: the attack an effect like Vengeance or Damnation answers each hit with shows the name and icon of that action, not a plain Attack.

Auto-attacks: when not made by you they say who makes them, like Attack Kweh, or the name of the enemy hitting you. The actions of your pet or chocobo end with its name too.

Merged hits: with the Merge options (General tab), an action that hits several targets shows one total and the number of hits. Critical hits are never merged: they show apart, with their look. Direct hits merge only among themselves.

Effects that do not take: an action of yours whose effect the enemy is immune to or resists in full says so after its name, like Leg Sweep Immune, in the color of misses. It goes where actions with no damage go.

Actions with no damage: an action of your job that deals no damage and heals nothing shows its icon and name: a dash, or a stun like Leg Sweep. One that only puts an effect on you does not: that effect is announced instead.

Effects like Bloodbath: what an attack heals you for shows as healing received.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.PositionalInline: Says whether the positional was hit in the message of the damage of the action, after its name, instead of in an alert of its own. The area and movement chosen above for the positional then do not apply: it goes where the damage goes.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Event.Positional: When you use an action that hits harder from the rear or the flank of its target, says whether you hit it from there. Choose its area and movement here, or show it in the damage message with the option below. Its look is in the Highlights tab.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Highlight.Positi: Gives the alert of a positional that was hit a look of its own. Off: it uses the font and size of its area, in green.
Gives the alert of a positional that was missed a look of its own. Off: it uses the font and size of its area, in red.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.MergeHeals.Help: An action that heals several targets at once shows a single total with the number of heals. Off: one message per target healed.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.ShowHealTargets: Show who my healing is for
The healing you give ends with the name of who it heals, in brackets. Merged healing has several targets and names none: turn off Merge healing on several targets to see each one.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Event.ActionUsed: An action of your job that deals no damage, heals nothing and applies no effect, like a dash. The game shows no text for these.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Area.Anchor.Star: Left: messages start at the area position and grow to the right.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Area.Anchor.Midd: Center: messages are centered on the area position.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Area.Anchor.End: Right: messages end at the area position and grow to the left.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Highlight.Animat: Kind of animation. Choosing one lists its animations on the right and plays the first of them.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Cooldowns.Hint: Click to turn on or off. Lit: announced. Hover to see the name.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Colors.Help: One color for each kind of text. Click a color to open the color picker.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Order.None: No event is sent to this area. Choose where each event goes in the Events tab.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Preview.Hint: Sample text is on. Drag the box of each area to move it. Press ? for help.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.MergeHits.Help: An attack that hits several targets at once shows a single total with the number of hits.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.IncludePets.Help: What your pet or chocobo deals is shown as outgoing.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.ShowDefended.Hel: Damage that was blocked, parried or resisted says so after the number, like -270 (parried). Off, only the number shows.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Mitigation.Help: Whether the damage you take ends with how much of it your damage reduction took off, and how: only the percent, like -270 (-30%), or with the word, like -270 (-30% mitigated). It is worked out from the effects active at that moment, as the actions that give them describe them.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Font.Help: Font of all messages. The size is set for each area, in the Areas tab.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Area.Enabled.Hel: Off: these events are left to the game's own fly text.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Area.OffsetX.Hel: Pixels to the right (positive) or left (negative) of the center of the screen.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Area.OffsetY.Hel: Pixels below (positive) or above (negative) the center of the screen.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Area.Anchor.Help: Which point of each message sits on the area position. 0: the message starts there and grows to the right. 50: centered. 100: it ends there and grows to the left.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Area.Height.Help: Pixels a message travels before it disappears.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Area.FontSize.He: Size of the text of this area. Highlighted messages (special hits, cooldown alerts) use their own size, set in the Highlights and Cooldowns tabs.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Area.Duration.He: Time a message stays on screen, in seconds.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Area.MinAmount.H: Damage and healing under this amount is not shown, neither here nor by the game. 0 shows everything.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Area.Style.Help: Path the messages of this area follow: a straight line, a curve that bows to one side, or Static (they stay in place and fade, piling up as more arrive).
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Order: Order of each message in this area
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Order.Help: Left to right order of the parts of the messages of this area. The arrows move a part and the eye hides or shows it. Only the parts used by the events sent to this area are listed. Each area has its own order.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Part.Name: Action name
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.ShowFading.Help: Buffs and debuffs are announced when they end (- name) as well as when they start (+ name).
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Event.Area.Help: Area this event scrolls in: Outgoing (right of your character), Incoming (left) or Center (under it).
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Event.DamageDeal: Damage you, your pet or your damage over time deal, with misses.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Event.DamageTake: Damage you receive, with what you dodge.
Healing you receive, from yourself or from others.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Event.Mp.Help: MP you recover from actions and effects.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Event.BuffOnMe.H: A beneficial effect starts or ends on you, whoever gave it.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Event.BuffOnOthe: A beneficial effect you put on someone else starts.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Event.DebuffOnMe: A harmful effect starts or ends on you.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Event.DebuffOnEn: A harmful effect of yours starts or ends on an enemy.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Event.Cooldown.H: Announces when one of the actions ticked below is ready to use again.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Cooldowns.Help: Click an action to turn its alert on or off: lit, its cooldown is announced; dimmed, it is not. The list is that of the job you had when this window was opened.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Cooldowns.None: No actions with a cooldown were found. Log in with a combat job and open this window again.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Command.Help: Opens or closes the Goblin Battle Text settings.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Event.Motion.Hel: How this event moves: scrolling upwards, scrolling downwards, or Static (it stays in place and fades). An area whose path is Static keeps all its events still.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.CooldownOrder.He: Left to right order of the parts of a cooldown alert. The eye hides or shows a part.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Help.Title: Help
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Help.Overview.Te:
Goblin Battle Text replaces the numbers that float over whoever is hit with text shown around the center of the screen, where your character stands, so you never lose sight of it. The game's own numbers for those events are hidden, so nothing appears twice.

There are three areas:
- Outgoing, to the right of your character: what you do.
- Incoming, to the left: what happens to you.
- Center, under your character: effects that start or end, and cooldowns.

Every kind of event can be sent to any of the three areas, or turned off.

Open this window with /gbt or from the tweak card in GoblinTweaks. While it is open, sample text is shown so you can see each change at once, and each area has a box with its name that you can drag to move it. Settings are saved automatically, and each character has its own: a character seen for the first time starts with a copy of the ones you had. The name under the title of this window says whose they are.

The button at the bottom right, held down, puts the tab you are looking at back to its defaults.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Help.General.Tex:
Merge damage / healing on several targets: an area attack or heal shows one total with the number of hits. Each has its own switch.

Show who my healing is for: the healing you give ends with the name of who it heals, when it is not merged.

Damage and healing over time: the game sends one tick per target with the sum of everyone's. When others have theirs on the same target, yours is shown as an estimate, with ~ before it.

Shorten large numbers: 12.3K instead of 12,345.

Include my pet and chocobo: their damage counts as yours.

Show blocked, parried and resisted: whether such a hit says so after its number.

Mitigated: whether damage you take ends with how much of it was taken off, with only the percent, like -270 (-30%), or with the word too, like -270 (-30% mitigated). It counts the effects on you that reduce the damage you take (Rampart, Damnation, Kerachole...) and those on whoever hit you that lower the damage it deals (Reprisal, Feint, Addle...), each with the percent the description of its action gives; several multiply, as in the game. Blocks, parries, barriers and anything with no percent in an action description are not counted.

Font: the font of all messages. The size is set for each area, in the Areas tab.

Colors: one for each kind of text: damage dealt, damage taken, healing, misses and dodges, MP gained, actions with no damage, and buffs and debuffs (one color when they start and another when they end). Click a color to open the color picker: Confirm applies it, Default puts back the original color, Cancel leaves it as it was.

The colors of critical and direct hits are in the Highlights tab, and those of the cooldown alert in the Cooldowns tab.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Help.Areas.Title: Areas tab
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Help.Areas.Text:
Choose the area at the top: Outgoing, Incoming or Center. The three have the same settings, and the Restore button only restores the one you are looking at. The cog next to them copies the look of the area to another one.

Show this area: off, its events go back to the game's own text.

Position X and Y: where the area is, in pixels from the center of the screen. Negative is left or up. Drag the box of the area on screen, move the slider, or set the exact number with + and -.

Alignment: 0, messages start at the area position and grow to the right. 50, centered. 100, they end there and grow to the left. The three buttons set those values.

Scroll distance, Font size and Duration (in seconds).

Minimum amount: smaller damage and healing is not shown at all.

Messages at once: how many show at the same time, 1 to 15. When one more arrives, the oldest disappears.

Path: straight, curved to one side, or Static (messages stay in place and fade).

Order of each message: the arrows move a part earlier or later and the eye hides or shows it. Only the parts used by the events sent to the area are listed.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Help.Events.Text:
One row per kind of event, with three settings:

- The checkbox turns the event on or off. Off, the game shows it as usual.
- Area: Outgoing, Incoming or Center.
- Movement: upwards, downwards or Static.

The events: Damage dealt and Damage taken (with misses and dodges), Healing on allies, Healing received (with what effects like Bloodbath heal you for), MP gained, Buff on me, Debuff on me, Buff I give, Debuff on enemy, and Action with no damage (your dashes and other actions the game shows no text for).

Announce effects that end: buffs and debuffs show + name when they start and also - name when they wear off.

Messages never cross. When an area has events going up and events going down, each direction takes one half of the area and starts from its middle: up from there upwards, down from there downwards. Static events pile up just outside the scrolling path. If the halves feel short, raise the scroll distance of the area.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Help.Cooldowns.T:
Cooldown alerts tell you when an action is ready to use again, like "Fast Blade ready now!". They are off until you tick the checkbox at the top. Next to it you choose the area and how the alert moves.

Own look for the alert: its font, size, animation, intensity and the color of the "ready now!" text. Off, the alert uses the font and size of its area, in white. The action name always has its own color.

Order of the cooldown alert: its three parts (icon, action name, "ready now!" text). The arrows move a part and the eye hides it.

Actions of your current job: click one to turn its alert on or off (lit: announced). Hover to see its name, or type part of it in the search box.

Which actions are there: those of your job at your level with a cooldown of their own of 5 seconds or more, not the global one. Actions that share a cooldown (an action and its upgrade) count once, and the mudras of a ninja are left out. The alert comes when the cooldown ends; with charges, when all of them are back. The list is that of the job you had when the window was opened: after changing job, close and open it again.

Procs are not in this list. An effect that makes an action available shows as Buff on me.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Defaults.Help: Hold down to put every setting of the tab you are looking at back to its default. In the Areas tab, only the area you are looking at. The other tabs are not touched.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Highlight.Critic: Gives critical hits (marked with !) their own look. Off: they look like any other hit of their area.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Highlight.Direct: Gives direct hits their own look. Off: they look like any other hit of their area.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Highlight.Critic: Gives critical direct hits (marked with !!) their own look. Off: they look like any other hit of their area.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Highlight.Cooldo: Gives cooldown alerts their own look. Off: they use the font and size of their area, with the text in white.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Highlight.Font.H: Font of this kind of message, in place of the general one.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Highlight.Animat: What the message does when it appears: first the kind of animation, then the animation. There are 35; the sample text plays the one you pick, so try them.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Highlight.FontSi: Size of this kind of message, in place of that of its area.
Choose at the top what to set: critical hits (!), direct hits, critical direct hits (!!), and the alerts of a positional that was hit or missed. Each has a look of its own. The look of the cooldown alert is in the Cooldowns tab.

Positional alerts: when you use an action that hits harder from the rear or the flank (Gekko, Kasha, Gibbet...), an alert says whether you hit it from there. True North counts as hit. Turn them on or off, and choose their area, in the Events tab.

- Checkbox: off, the message looks like any other of its area.
- Colors: one for the damage you deal and one for the damage you take; critical hits have a third one for healing, the only other thing that can be critical.
- Font and Font size, in place of those of the area.
- Animation, played when the message appears: choose its kind in the first list and the animation in the second.
- Intensity: strength of the animation, 0 to 300, 100 being normal.

Gentle: Pop, Shake, Pulse, Flash.
Impacts: Slam, Quake, Earthquake, Stomp, Crush, Shockwave, Meteor, Fury.
Size: Bounce, Zoom, Stretch, Explode, Heartbeat.
Rotation: Swing, Rattle, Spin, Tornado.
Movement: Drop, Launch, Dash, Recoil.
Light: Blaze, Thunder, Ignite, Ember, Frost, Venom, Blood, Radiance, Shadow, Strobe.

While this tab is open, the sample text only shows the kind chosen at the top.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Highlight.Intens: Strength of the animation, in percent: how large it grows, how far it moves or tilts, how bright or dark it gets. 100 is the normal strength, 0 leaves the message still.
Tweaks.GoblinBattleText.Area.MaxMessages: How many messages this area shows at the same time, 1 to 15. When one more arrives, the oldest disappears.
